F11.title: Portabilidade, SDK e documentação
F11.gate: Exportar e importar em staging mantém IDs; plugin de exemplo adiciona tipo sem patch do core.
F11.why_gate_is_open: All five tasks are complete and the gate is met at the level of the code: an exported file keeps the identifiers it carried because the document's field identifiers are its own, and the example plugin adds a field type without patching the core, proven end to end and now documented. The one thing the gate names that this environment cannot exercise is the word 'staging': moving a configuration between two stores needs two stores, and this one has a single site. The merchant documentation is written, and it says which screens exist and which are still placeholders — the Import/Export section among them.
F11.way_forward: F12 is the functional matrix and the browser work: classic and Blocks, HPOS on and off, payment gateways by version, and the end-to-end order that closes the observation gaps every earlier phase recorded. Two things it needs that this environment does not have are already named as blockers — a gateway with sandbox credentials (SANDBOX-PAYMENT) and a second store for the transfer run — and both are external configuration rather than implementation.
F11.detail: WCCS-056 delivered export, preview and import, and reused what F03 had already built rather than growing a second diff: the preview returns the same SchemaDiff the publish panel reads. The preview and the import are one inspection read twice — one returns the report, the other writes it — because two paths that decided separately would disagree about what a file means, and the disagreement would appear as a change the merchant never saw. The file is validated by the same definition validator the editor and the publish route use, so a document the interface would refuse cannot arrive as a file; the proof demonstrates it with a field of a type that does not exist. The limits are checked before the file becomes a document and the refusal names the numbers it exceeded. Conflicts are the revision: a file carries where it came from, a file from another revision is reported as a conflict, and the import writes into the draft through the same compare-and-swap the editor uses. The rollback is not a feature and did not need to be one — an import is a draft, nothing reaches the checkout until it is published, publishing keeps a revision and restore brings one back as a new revision — and the proof walks that whole path rather than inventing a second undo, because a second history disagrees with the first the moment one of them is restored. The secrets clause is an absence asserted over the file: token, nonce, password, secret, api key, authorization, wp-content and the plugin path are all searched for, and the envelope is asserted to have exactly the five keys of the document. Two defects were found and both are worth recording. The first was real and in the import: the shared report removed the document before answering, so the import wrote a null — invisible until the proof drove the route instead of the class, which is the difference between testing the piece and testing the path. The second was the rollback's starting state, written straight into the slot and therefore never in the history: a state the store never recorded is a state it cannot return to, and the harness now publishes through the publish path. The option count needed the same pre-clearing correction three other proofs already carry, which makes it a pattern rather than an accident. Two gaps are named: the Import/Export section of the administration still renders the placeholder it has rendered since the shell was built, so the file is reachable by a client and not yet by a merchant, and version migration is structured but unexercised because version 1 is the only version that exists. WCCS-057 delivered the limited migrator, and the limitation is the task. Section 21 asks for the structures proven in the source and a report for everything else, and forbids importing Premium configuration by assumption: the mapping table was therefore not written from memory of how a checkout field editor usually works but read in an installation of the source, and every entry of that reading is recorded in the class with the file it came from — the three option keys, the shape of a field entry, the encoded choices, and the types the source actually uses. The version those structures were read in is recorded and does not match the version the planning referenced: the installation declares 2.1.5 and the ZIP the planning attached declared 2.2.0, so the adapter states both rather than smoothing them together, because a mapping verified in one version is a mapping about that version. Silence is what the acceptance forbids, so a type this plugin does not have is refused with the type named rather than becoming a text box — the tempting default and the one that loses data without telling anybody — a setting with no equivalent is reported beside its field, a key nobody declared is reported as what a later version of the source looks like from here, and an entry that is not a mapping is reported as such. The invariant that closes the clause is that every field ends in one of the two lists, with the lines about settings counted apart from the fields; the first version of that assertion compared counts of different things. With no source installed the adapter does nothing and says so, because reading options that are not there returns empties and empties are not a migration. The result is a valid document and the same envelope WCCS-056 introduced, so a migration is previewed before anything is stored, and the file says what produced it. The proof found a real defect in the section mapping: the first version wrote the source's own words through, producing sections the shared validator refused with section_missing_title and section_unknown_location, because the source's additional section is this plugin's order location and this plugin's sections carry a title. It is the second time in the phase that the shared validation caught a new layer — a document the interface would refuse cannot arrive as a file, and cannot leave a migration either. Two things are named: running the migration against a store that has the source installed needs that store, and historical values are not migrated, which the planning says and the report repeats. WCCS-058 completed the example field type, and the task was not about the example: both adapters decided what they could draw from closed maps they own, so a type contributed by another plugin was offered by the picker and drawable by neither checkout — a contract that existed only on paper. The correction was not to add the type to an internal list, which is a special case rather than an SDK, but to let a type declare which existing control draws it: supports() gained `control`, and both adapters honour the declaration instead of consulting a list of their own. The declaration is a choice among controls that already exist — a select is still a select, and what makes a membership code a membership code is the validation the contributing plugin wrote — and a type that declares nothing is still drawn by nothing, asserted against both the core text type and a type that does not exist. All four surfaces the acceptance names are asserted through the paths a store uses: the type registers through the published hook with its key read from the example's own constant, the catalogue route the picker reads offers it with its label, source and declared control, the classic adapter accepts it and the field reaches the checkout field array as text, the Blocks adapter calls it controlled and the renderer publishes it with the control that the bundle uses to choose a component, and a value goes through the example's own normalize and validate before being written to an order and read back. The proof confirmed rather than assumed that the value pipeline already calls the registered type: three of its four failures were its own expectations written from outside the contract it was testing — it expected lower case where the example upper-cases, and used a value the example accepts as its refusal case — and the fourth was a real gap in the harness, which published a document with no section and therefore no location for the renderer to put the field in. That the field is invisible without its section is the renderer behaving correctly. WCCS-059 documented the contracts this plugin publishes, and the documentation is guarded rather than trusted: a unit test reads every published hook out of the source and requires it to be named in the document, and reads every hook the document names and requires it to exist. That guard found a real gap on its first run — wccs_core_fields_inventory, published since F03 and documented nowhere — and it found three defects in itself, all of the same family: it first treated option names as hooks, then read the constant's name instead of its value, and then flagged identifiers in prose, which is why it now reads only the lines that show the call. The document answers the acceptance clause by clause: the order in which the registries are built and the client publishes its registry, fifteen hooks with their signatures and what each returns, six versioned contracts and where each lives, a four-rule deprecation policy with the warning travelling in code rather than only in prose, and the React component an extension contributes. That last clause is code and not a paragraph: the bundle publishes window.wccsBlocksFields before it draws anything, componentFor() consults it before the components it ships, and a type that declares a custom control whose component is not registered is not drawn but reported — so a contributed type can now bring its own component rather than only choose one of the controls that exist, which is the other side of WCCS-058. Two things are named: no contract is deprecated today, so the policy is unexercised, and the example's client-side file that would register a component does not exist yet even though the mechanism and its documentation do. WCCS-060 wrote the merchant's guide, and its honesty is what makes it usable: each task says where it is done today, and where a screen does not exist it says so and gives the route that does. The five tasks the acceptance names are covered — the PF/PJ flow through the presets and the rule editor, uploads with the two facts a merchant has to know before using them (the files are private and the feature disables itself when the hosting serves that folder) and the three retention rules, the layout through the opt-in switch and the token file, restore through three distinct paths that are not the same thing (restoring a revision, importing a file into the draft, and a conflict that refuses rather than overwrites), and diagnostics that read the mode and its reason, the gateways with their homologation state, and what the store supports per field type. Privacy points at WordPress's own tools and says what the store's answer contains. The guide ends by stating what it does not promise, which is the part that keeps it true: nothing requires editing code, no compatibility with every gateway is promised, and no legal conformity is claimed. It also records the gap plainly rather than routing around it — the Import/Export section of the administration still renders the placeholder it has rendered since the shell was built, so the three routes are reachable by an authenticated client and not yet by a merchant.

defects_found_and_fixed: The import route wrote a null document: the shared inspection removed the document from the report before answering, and the import used that same report to write. Found because the proof drives the route rather than the class — a test of SchemaTransfer alone would have passed. The preview now removes the document from its own answer and the import removes it after writing.

The rollback proof started from a document written straight into the published slot, which is a state the store never recorded and therefore one the history does not hold, so there was nothing to restore. The harness now publishes through the publish path, which is what writes history — and the assertion that failed was the one demanding a rollback that works.

The diff assertion expected identifiers where SchemaDiff returns whole definitions, and the option-count assertion compared against an environment a previous failed run had left behind — the third proof in this session to need the pre-clearing correction, which has become a pattern rather than an accident.

The migrator wrote the source's own words into the sections: `location` carried `additional`, which is not a location this plugin validates against, and the section carried `label` where the vocabulary requires `title`. The shared validator refused it with section_missing_title and section_unknown_location. Found because the proof validates what the migration produced rather than only that it produced something; the section mapping now translates, and an assertion requires billing/order.

The proof's own invariant compared counts of different things — fields against report lines, since a setting inside a field also produces a line. It now compares fields with fields, with the setting lines counted separately, which is what makes 'no field is dropped' a statement about fields.

A field type contributed by another plugin was invisible on both checkouts: the classic and Blocks adapters decided what they could draw from closed maps they own, so the picker offered the type and neither checkout could render it. Found by asking the two adapters about the example's key rather than by reading the code; the contract now lets a type declare which existing control draws it.

The Blocks payload type did not declare the new `control`, which tsc refused in three places — the type a component receives and the payload the server sends had drifted in the same commit that introduced the field. Corrected in the typedef, which is where the contract between the two halves is written down.

The proof's own expectations were wrong three times: it expected the example to lower-case where it upper-cases, used a value the example accepts as its refusal case, and read a provenance key (`origin`) the catalogue publishes as `source`. All three were written from outside the contract; the fourth failure was real and in the harness, which published a document with no section and therefore no location for the renderer.

The documentation guard found a hook nobody had documented: `wccs_core_fields_inventory`, published since F03 and named in no document. Found because the guard reads the hooks out of the source rather than from a list somebody maintains.

The guard itself was wrong three times in the same family: it treated option names as hooks (any constant whose value starts with wccs_), then read the constant's name instead of its value, which made every documented hook look phantom, and then flagged identifiers in prose. It now reads only constants whose name names a hook and only the lines that show the call — the convention the code already followed.

The client registry needed `wccsBlocksFields` declared in the globals type and the result of `tsc` refusing it, and a `no-shadow` refusal for naming the method `register` beside the module's own `register` export. Both are the same lesson as the payload typedef in WCCS-058: the two halves of a client contract drift in the commit that introduces them unless the declaration is written with the code.

Nothing was fixed in this task: it is documentation, and the only thing it changed is what a reader knows. The gap it records — the Import/Export screen existing as routes but not as a screen — was found by writing the instructions and refusing to write a step for a button that is not there.

F12.title: Hardening, acessibilidade e matriz final
F12.gate: Nenhum defeito crítico de pagamento, exposição de dados ou perda de configuração; matriz publicada.
F12.why_gate_is_open: Two of the phase's five tasks are done and one is blocked, and the ground under the remaining three moved at the start of WCCS-063: the store has a published Blocks checkout page and nine published products, and the host has Chromium, Google Chrome and Playwright. Every phase from F04 onwards justified a missing observation with the absence of a page or of a product, and that justification is not the store's state — it is recorded as OBSERVATION-SURFACE-CORRECTION. The classic checkout page is still absent, which is what CLASSIC-TEST-SURFACE records, so the Classic rows of the matrix remain unobservable. The gate itself is unchanged: no critical defect in payment, in data exposure or in configuration loss, and the matrix published — and the payment rows still need a gateway with credentials.
F12.way_forward: WCCS-063 can now be executed rather than recorded: publish a document with a field, open the Blocks checkout with Playwright at the five widths, and read focus, zoom and reduced motion from the rendered page. WCCS-065 can place a real order, which the nine products make possible. What cannot be opened is the classic checkout, whose page does not exist, and no payment row can be homologated without SANDBOX-PAYMENT.
F12.detail: WCCS-061 assembled the seven security classes into one suite, and the value of that is the framing rather than the individual assertions: IDOR, XSS, CSRF, token replay, payloads, MIME and concurrency were each exercised where the feature that owns them was built, and a class asserted on its own is an assertion about a feature while the seven together are an assertion about the product. The suite asserts that a store user without permission on a particular order is refused with the same answer a missing order gets, because two different answers would be an enumeration oracle; that one stored value containing a script tag is escaped on all three surfaces that can show it — the customer's page, the staff screen and the e-mail body; that a submission with no nonce and one with a wrong nonce write nothing and that a write route without a session is refused; that binding a token that is not the owner's binds nothing and that repeating the submission is idempotent; that an oversized payload is refused before it is parsed and one from a newer format version is refused rather than partly read; that the MIME rule decides by what the file is rather than by what its name claims; and that a writer holding a revision that is no longer current is refused rather than allowed to overwrite. What the suite could not produce is stated rather than simulated: no multipart upload was performed, so the MIME class is asserted on the rule that decides it and the refusal of a shell script named document.txt remains where it was exercised, in WCCS-042; no concurrent PHP process was used, so concurrency is the compare-and-swap the writes actually take with two writers in one request; and the download refusal is named with a pointer to WCCS-044 because repeating it needs a stored upload and this store accepts none. Four of the suite's own assertions were wrong before it passed and all four are the same family: a request described as anonymous still carried the administrator session, so the 200 was right and the assertion was wrong; the harness did not clear the slots it owns before measuring, which is the fifth proof in this session to need that correction; the concurrency assertion required the first writer to win, which depends on the starting state rather than on what the store guarantees; and two assertions used methods that do not exist, invented from outside — the first died silently, the sixth time in this session that a harness died without a word. WCCS-062 published the functional matrix, and the task's own criterion decided its shape: the planning says the report states what passed, what failed and what was not tested, and adds that a compiled artefact, an HPOS badge or a quiet console are not payment homologation. The matrix therefore has three states and never two, and 'not tested' is the most frequent — which is the finding rather than a gap in the document. Fifty-four integration harnesses exercise the seams of this plugin against the installed WooCommerce and none of them is a customer in a browser, so the Classic and Blocks rows are covered at the seam and the row that says 'a customer filling a form' is not covered anywhere. The order-storage group is covered for HPOS authoritative and not for HPOS disabled, because toggling the store's order storage is a site setting outside this plugin's root; the cart-type group needs products and this store has none, which is the same blockage that kept the Store API checkout round trip unexecuted since F07; and every gateway row is untested because no gateway is enabled and none has credentials, which is why the homologation record is empty and all seven answer undecided. The matrix ends by naming the four external actions that would close the missing rows — products, a sandbox gateway, a browser and an order-storage toggle — and each of them is already recorded as a blocker or an open decision rather than discovered here. The task is recorded as partially completed and blocked, because its acceptance names gateways registered by version and that clause cannot be met in this environment. WCCS-063 was opened by checking the environment before writing anything, and the check is the finding: the store has a published checkout page at /finalizar-compra/ and nine published products, and the host has Chromium, Google Chrome and Playwright. Phases from F04 to F11 recorded 'no checkout page' and 'no product' as the reason an observation was not made, and at least the second of those is not this store's state — the first is half true, because the page exists but is a Blocks checkout, which is what CLASSIC-TEST-SURFACE means. The correction is recorded as its own entry rather than folded into a phase, because it is not about a phase: it is about a fact that several phases relied on. It also means the browser observation was never attempted rather than attempted and failed, and the next step is to make it: publish a document with a field and drive the Blocks checkout with Playwright at the five widths the acceptance names.

defects_found_and_fixed: No product defect was found by the security suite. Four of its own assertions were wrong before it passed: a request described as anonymous still carried the administrator session, so the 200 it received was correct; the harness did not clear the schema slots it owns before measuring, the fifth proof in this session to need that correction; the concurrency assertion required the first writer to win, which is a property of the starting state rather than of the store, and now asserts the guarantee that a writer holding a stale revision is refused; and two assertions called methods that do not exist (DownloadPolicy::refusal_status, UploadRules::ALLOWED_MIMES), invented from outside the code — the first died silently, the sixth silent harness death of the session.

open_decisions.question: Which declaration is authoritative for the value type a field holds: the valueSchema() the field type publishes, or the table ConditionValidator::definition_type() keeps by hand?

open_decisions.finding: They disagree today for one registered type. FileFieldType::valueSchema() returns array — a file field holds a list of attachments — while definition_type() maps the file type to string, so a rule using 'contains' on a file field is judged as a text comparison.
options: make the validator read the published valueSchema through the type registry, which is what its own docblock says the registry knows better for, at the cost of a static class gaining a registry dependency
keep the hand-written table and make it a rule that every registered type has to appear in it, at the cost of a list that a third-party type will not be on
open_decisions.why_not_settled_here: Both options change a contract rather than a branch, and no rule currently in the store depends on the answer: nothing is published and no condition has been evaluated. Settling it inside WCCS-032 would have been an implementation decision taken while proving something else.
open_decisions.evidence: Recorded in docs/validation/WCCS-032.md section 6, and observed by inspecting the two declarations rather than by a failing test, which is why no assertion was written for either answer.
open_decisions.recommendation: Decide it in WCCS-033, where the evaluators have to agree with the validator about what a value is — a parity task cannot be completed while the two sides disagree about the type of a list.
